clinician.trajectory_summary: A 44-year-old woman presented with a 3-month history of progressive pruritic rash involving extremities, oral cavity, and intertriginous areas (groin, abdomen, axillae, gluteal region). Physical examination revealed well-demarcated erythematous plaques with fragile vesicles consistent with necrolytic migratory erythema (NME). Skin biopsy confirmed NME with psoriasiform acanthosis, abrupt necrosis of upper epidermal layers, and necrolytic changes. Laboratory workup demonstrated marked hyperglucagonemia (720 ng/L, normal 40-130), elevated chromogranin A (243 ng/mL), hyperglycemia (132 mg/dL), and HbA1c 6.3% consistent with diabetes mellitus. CT imaging localized a 3-cm enhancing pancreatic head mass. The patient underwent surgical resection, with post-operative course complicated by pancreatic fistula that resolved non-operatively. Pathology of the resected specimen confirmed pancreatic neuroendocrine carcinoma with vascular and perineural invasion. Post-operatively, glucagon and glucose levels dropped dramatically, and cutaneous lesions resolved within one week.
